description.value: The study compared fMRI ROI data-aggregation measures as prognostic factors for relapse in abstinent alcohol-dependent individuals performing a cue-reactivity task, using linear regression to identify relapse-associated regions and Cox regression to evaluate survival outcomes.

spans.text: In this study, we compared the performance of different ROI data-aggregation measures, using survival analysis as an example for such analyses.

model_representation_notes.value: The linear regression did not account for right-censoring: abstinent patients were treated as if they had relapsed at the end of the follow-up period. It was used only exploratorily to identify relevant ROIs before applying Cox regression.

spans.text: In abstainers, “days until first severe relapse” are right-censored and equal the follow-up period (80 days). For this reason, the linear model we used is not statistically appropriate for our data because it treats abstinent patients as if they had relapsed. Despite this, we used it anyway to identify relevant brain regions on an exploratory basis.

Total scan time per patient was 12 min and 218 volumes were acquired in total.
Scanning was performed using a 1.5-T clinical whole-body tomography scanner (Magnetom VISION, Siemens, Erlangen, Germany) equipped with a standard quadrature head coil.

We acquired 24 slices every 3.3 s (4 mm thickness, 1 mm gap) using a standard echoplanar imaging (EPI) sequence (TR = 1.8 ms, TE = 66 ms, α = 90°) with an in-plane resolution of 64 × 64 pixels and a field of view (FOV) of 220 mm × 220 mm, resulting in a voxel size of 3.44 mm × 3.44 mm × 5 mm.
